system:
You are working out the chronology of a compulsory third party motor accident claim in New South Wales, from a list of things recorded about decided claims.

Divide the life of a claim into ordered PHASES, and place every recorded item in the phase at which the thing it measures COMES INTO EXISTENCE -- not when it is written down, and not when it is used.

Work out from each definition what the measured thing IS, and place it when that thing comes into being. Some definitions carry their own timing: a condition described as pre-existing is one the claimant had beforehand. Others do not, and for those you must reason about the claim.

Some entries are NOT OBSERVED. They have no column and no values, but they are real quantities the data traces only indirectly, and they must be placed too. Where an unobserved quantity has an observed indicator, place the unobserved thing when IT arose and the indicator when the OBSERVATION was made: an injury and the later discussion of that injury are different events. An indicator can never be earlier than the thing it indicates.

That distinction decides most of the hard cases:
  * A medical assessment performed years later measures a physical state that arose at the time of the injury. Ask when the QUANTITY was fixed, not when it was measured.
  * Something recorded in the final decision may describe a fact established long before it.
  * A procedural fact about how the claim was run belongs to the phase in which the claim was run, not to the injury.

Decide how many phases there are. Use as few as genuinely capture the order and no more; a phase containing one item is fine if that item really stands alone in time. Items that arise at the same stage belong in the same phase, and a phase may contain items that cause one another -- being contemporaneous is not being simultaneous.

For every item, say in one sentence WHEN the thing it measures came into existence. That sentence is the justification for its placement and will be recorded.
user:
Recorded about each decided claim:
  - Lump Sum: the total dollars awarded to the claimant
      [how recorded: read directly off the decision]
  - WPI %: whole person impairment as a percentage: a clinical assessment of the permanent impairment remaining once the claimant's condition has stabilised
      [how recorded: read directly off the decision]
  - Non-Economic Loss: dollars awarded for pain and suffering, as a component of the payout
      [how recorded: read directly off the decision]
  - Future Economic Loss: dollars awarded for loss of future earning capacity, as a component of the payout
      [how recorded: read directly off the decision]
  - Claimant Weekly Income: the claimant's weekly earnings before the accident
      [how recorded: read directly off the decision]
  - Claimant Age: the claimant's age in years at the date of injury
      [how recorded: read directly off the decision]
  - Claimant Gender: the claimant's recorded gender
      [how recorded: read directly off the decision]
  - Nature: which procedural route the claim took: approval of an agreed settlement, or a contested damages assessment
      [how recorded: read directly off the decision]
  - Injury Burden Intensity: the overall physical severity of the injuries the claimant sustained in the accident
      [how recorded: assigned by a language model scoring the written decision]
  - Treatment Burden: the extent of treatment, surgery and ongoing care the claimant underwent for those injuries
      [how recorded: assigned by a language model scoring the written decision]
  - Work Impact Severity: how much of the claimant's capacity to work was lost
      [how recorded: assigned by a language model scoring the written decision]
  - Legal Procedural Complexity: how straightforward or contested the components of the payout were to determine
      [how recorded: assigned by a language model scoring the written decision]
  - Psychological Injury Emphasis: how much the psychological damage was discussed in the court case
      [how recorded: assigned by a language model scoring the written decision]
      [this is the observed indicator of Psychological Injury]
  - Liability Clarity: how obvious it is who was at fault in the accident
      [how recorded: assigned by a language model scoring the written decision]
  - Causation Complexity: how straightforward it is to determine how much of the claimant's current physical health, psychological health, and ability to earn an income is due to the accident rather than to other causes
      [how recorded: assigned by a language model scoring the written decision]
  - Pre-existing Condition Salience: the physical and psychological health conditions the claimant had before the accident
      [how recorded: assigned by a language model scoring the written decision]
  - Psychological Injury: the psychological injury the claimant suffered as a result of the accident -- its actual severity, as distinct from how much it was discussed
      [NOT OBSERVED: no column, no values. Its only measured trace is Psychological Injury Emphasis]

Define the ordered phases of a claim, then place every item in one.

phases.name: Pre-Accident Conditions
phases.description: This phase includes the state of the claimant before the accident, specifically related to their health and income.

phases.name: Accident and Injury
phases.description: This phase involves the occurrence of the accident and the resulting injuries and burdens.

phases.name: Claim Initiation
phases.description: This phase involves the initial setting up of the claim, including determining procedural aspects like fault and pre-claim conditions.

phases.name: Claim Assessment
phases.description: This phase includes all evaluations and assessments required for the decision on the claim, covering medical assessments and deciding procedural complexity.

phases.name: Claim Decision
phases.description: The final phase where the decision is made about the payout, including amounts for different loss components.

assignments.when_it_arises: The claimant's weekly income existed before the accident.
The claimant's age is determined at the date of injury, which is a pre-existing condition.
The claimant's gender is a constant attribute existing before the accident.
Pre-existing conditions are those existing before the accident.
The intensity of the injury burden arises at the time of the accident.
The treatment burden arises following the injuries sustained in the accident.
The psychological injury itself arises at the time of the accident.
Liability clarity arises in the initial stages of claim processing.
Causation complexity is identified at the stage of assessing claim validity and setting up the claim.
The WPI % is determined once the claimant's condition stabilizes, which is during the assessment phase.
The severity of the work impact is assessed during claim evaluation.
Legal procedural complexity is assessed during the claim processing and assessment phase.
The emphasis on psychological injury is determined during the assessment phase when evaluating the claims and case.
The procedural route is determined during the claim assessment phase.
The lump sum as the total payout is decided in the final decision phase.
The non-economic loss is awarded as part of the final decision on compensation.
The future economic loss is calculated and awarded during the final decision phase.
